params.body:
Three things went wrong in a test call:

1. **A site landed as loose words.** The conversation understood the site, but the sheet showed the words as spoken instead of the site. Only an exact code or an exact name linked it, so a name written with other capitals, accents or dashes went in as `site_description`.
2. **Nothing was confirmed.** The prompt said never to repeat what it understood, so a site or an hour understood wrongly went on the sheet without him hearing it.
3. **Two blocks of hours became one.** "Van 9 tot 12 en van 1 tot 5" became 9 to 5, which counts the lunch as worked.

This PR is built on #84 (not merged yet) and contains it. Merging this one is enough.

## What changes

**The prompt:**
- **Confirming.** A new section, "Vraag of je hem goed begrepen hebt". The model confirms, in one short sentence each, before it goes on:
  - the site, always, with name and municipality ("Stabil in Zulte, heb ik dat goed?");
  - the hours as it writes them;
  - anything it linked to a name that sounds different from what he said, or is unsure of.

  If he says no, it asks what it was. Anything it heard clearly and takes over literally (the work done, a quantity) it does not read back. On closing, it says in one sentence what is on the sheet (site and hours) and asks whether it may be handed in. `ConversationTest` pinned the old "the voice does not confirm" rule; it now pins this narrower one.
- **Blocks of hours.** "Van 9 tot 12 en van 1 tot 5" is two lines on the same site (09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00), never one block. The gap is not filled in as a break unless he talks about a break. Hours without morning or afternoon follow a working day: "1 tot 5" is 13:00 to 17:00. The tool's `lines` description says the same.
- **Site codes.** A site that is in the list is always written with its `site_code`, also when he says the name differently. If the model does not recognise it literally, it looks it up with `opties_opzoeken` (each result starts with the code), confirms it with him, and writes the code.

**The writer (`findSite`), still exactly one site or none:**
- a code written in front of the name ("P-20250310 Verkaveling Ter Beke") links that site;
- the same name written differently links it too: capitals, accents, dashes and spacing are ignored.

A name that is only close ("Ter Beek") or that fits two sites ("Kerkplein") still links nothing.

**Transcription hint (`Jargon`).** It now uses the offered sites from #82, so a worker without history of his own gets the busiest sites as recognition hints.

## Tests

- `ConfirmAndMatchTest` covers:
  - the prompt asks for confirmation and keeps blocks apart;
  - two blocks on one site give two lines and 7 hours, not 8;
  - three spellings with a code or other accents land on the site;
  - "Kerkplein" (two sites) and "Ter Beek" (close) land on none.
- `ConversationTest` follows the new confirmation rule.
- Full suite 263/263, JS 15/15.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
